name: Executive order of June 30, 1883 setting apart the Deer Creek reserve for the Bois Forte Band
nations: Bois Forte Band of Chippewa (Minnesota Chippewa Tribe)
promises: This was an executive order, not a treaty. Royce records that the President set apart the Deer Creek reserve, Township 62 North, Range 25 West of the fourth principal meridian, in accordance with the treaty of April 7, 1866.
landTaken: None by this order: it set land apart (Royce area 484).
today: Royce records that under the Nelson Act agreement of November 12, 1889 the Bois Forte and Deer Creek Chippewa ceded the Bois Forte and Deer Creek reservations; that cession has its own record (cession-1889-11-12-chippewa-bois-forte-band). The Bois Forte Band counts Deer Creek, in Itasca County, as one of the three sectors of its reservation today and says no Band members live there.

nationVoice.summary: The Band's history says its reservation has three sectors, Nett Lake, Vermilion and Deer Creek, that the Nett Lake and Deer Creek regions were established in the 1866 treaty, and that no Band members currently live at Deer Creek.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 912, executive order of June 30, 1883, Bois Forte
A Brief Summary of Bois Forte History

openQuestions: The order created a reserve; no finding treats it as a breach. What became of Deer Creek under the 1889 Nelson Act is covered by cession-1889-11-12-chippewa-bois-forte-band.
The order was read only in Royce's summary.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Chippewa, Bois Forte, Bois Forte Deer Creek; Docket 18-D (39 Ind. Cl. Comm. 300, 1977) quotes the 1866 treaty promise of a township at the mouth of Deer Creek while valuing the 1866 cession, with no finding about this 1883 reserve; nothing new.
